'''''Rosa gigantea''''' is a species of [[rose]] native to northeast [[India]], northern [[Myanmar]] and [[southwest China]] ([[Yunnan]]) in the foothills of the [[Himalaya]] at 1000–1500 m altitude. It is sometimes considered to be a [[variety (botany)|variety]] of ''[[Rosa odorata]]'', as ''R. odorata'' var. ''gigantea''.<ref>{{cite book |chapter-url=http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=200011293 |chapter=''Rosa odorata'' var. ''gigantea'' |title=Flora of China |volume=9 |author1=Gu Cuizhi (Ku Tsue-chih)|author2=Kenneth R. Robertson}}</ref>

As its name suggests, it is the largest species of rose, climbing 20 m or more into the crowns of other [[tree]]s by means of its stout, hooked thorns, and with a trunk up to 50 cm diameter. The [[leaf|leaves]] are semi-evergreen, 15–25 cm long, pinnate, with usually 7 leaflets, each leaflet 4–8 cm long. The [[flower]]s are white, creamy or yellow, the largest of any wild rose, 10–14 cm diameter. The [[rose hip|hips]] are yellow or orange, 2.5–3.5 cm diameter, hard, and often lasting through the winter into the following spring, often still present at the same time as the next years' flowers.

Another rose, described from [[Manipur]] in 1888 as ''R. macrocarpa'' and ''R. xanthocarpa'' by [[George Watt (botanist)|Sir George Watt]], an authority on [[India]]n [[rose]]s, is now generally considered to be the same species as ''R. gigantea''. The distinct characteristics claimed for ''R. macrocarpa'' (deeper yellow flowers, larger foliage with 4 to 7 leaflets and large yellow fruits) are not consistent.

After [[Whole genome sequencing|gene sequencing]] was carried out in 2018, it was found that ''[[Rosa roxburghii]]'' is closely related to ''Rosa odorata var. gigantea''.<ref name="Wang">{{cite journal |last1=Wang |first1=Qian |last2=Hu |first2=Huan |last3=An |first3=Jiaxing |last4=Bai |first4=Guohui |last5=Ren |first5=Qunli |last6=Liu |first6=Jianguo |title=Complete chloroplast genome sequence of Rosa roxburghii and its phylogenetic analysis |journal=Mitochondrial DNA Part B |date=2018 |volume=3 |issue=1 |pages=149–150 |doi=10.1080/23802359.2018.1431074 |doi-access=free |pmc=7800368 }}</ref>
